newsitem.title: USA: NY Gov to seek waiver from Food Stamp rules--paper.
newsitem.headline: NY Gov to seek waiver from Food Stamp rules--paper.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki plans to request a waiver from federal workfare rules that starting Saturday require adults to work in exchange for Food Stamps, New York Times reported Friday.
The governor, who announced he would make the request during an interview on WCBS-AM radio, noted that a number of counties throughout the state do not yet have workfare programs up and running.

Previously, the Pataki Administration sought a narrower waiver that would apply only to areas where unemployment rates are above 10 percent -- a standard that presently would only qualify two areas, Bronx and Hamilton County, in the southern Adirondacks.

The paper said Pataki, who has trumpeted the state's economic revival under his rule, was reluctant to apply for a wider waiver as this would conflict with his Administration's contention that jobs are available for those who want them.
Advocates for the poor have urged the governor to apply for a broader waiver to protect an estimated 100,000 able-bodied adults who now get federally funded Food Stamps.

Many of them are at risk of losing their benefits in the next three months unless Pataki seeks the waiver. The new federal rules only allow able-bodied adults who do not have children to get three months of food stamp benefits a year if they are under 50 years old and not working at least 20 hours a week, the paper said.
